title: Domain Names
drDigitalIntro:
A domain name is the address of a website — and the ending tells you something about the site.
• .com means a commercial (business) website. Most businesses use it: google.com, amazon.com.
• .org means an organization, usually non-profit: wikipedia.org, redcross.org.
• .gov means a government site: usa.gov. .edu means a school or university.
• .example (in our practice browser) is a made-up domain, like a fake street in a training video.
• Every domain is unique — there is only one google.com in the world, just like there is only one street address per building.
• Watch out for tricks: citylibrary.example looks real, but citylibrary.example.evil-site.net is actually owned by evil-site.net — the real domain is always the last two parts before the first slash.

playgroundTask.goal: Visit a .com and a .org and notice the different endings

steps.say: Google.com ends in .com — a commercial site. Type google.com in the address bar and press Enter.
Wikipedia.org ends in .org — a non-profit organization. Type wikipedia.org and press Enter to see the different ending.

drDigitalSuccess: You visited a .com (business) and a .org (organization). The ending after the dot is called the TLD — top-level domain. It gives you a clue about who runs the site.
drDigitalHint: Type each address in the bar and press Enter. Notice how the ending changes: .com then .org.
